note: The fuzzer-controlled raw input bytes are installed as the in-memory HAProxy configuration buffer.
The in-memory config, including embedded NUL bytes, is passed to the configuration parser with its byte length.
The parser keeps a byte-position cursor into the fuzzer-provided configuration content.
Each logical configuration line is copied from the length-delimited input into the heap line buffer.
The copy preserves embedded NUL bytes from the raw input, so C-string operations will see a shorter line than the byte-delimited parser position.
The input cursor advances past the full byte-delimited line even when an embedded NUL occurs before the newline.
The parser computes the visible line end using strlen, so an embedded NUL makes end point before the newline actually copied into the heap line buffer.
Because strlen stopped at the embedded NUL rather than the copied newline, the parser records the line as missing its LF.
The truncated C-string view is tokenized into the outline/args arrays.
Tokenization emits a terminating NUL for the parsed argument list based on the shortened C-string view.

The parser fills trailing argument pointers from the output position computed from the shortened line, which can reference the byte after the allocated output when the output buffer is only sized to the prior measured length.
